notes.title: Steam Summer Sale, Bug Fixes and The End of the Hipster Bun.
notes.content:
Hello Everyone,
I've just set the latest build live containing a big bunch of bug fixes for things reported by players.
As always, thank you so much to everyone who have sent in comments, bugs and suggestions. You're awesome!

The main fixes in this build are:
[list]
[*]Fixed loading of technology save game file from old save games.
[*]Fixed bug where the floor tiles wouldn't change when you have more than one area unlocked.
[*]Fix some missing animations which caused a logic issue with staff using equipment. Added a default animation for the staff to prevent any possible similar issues.
[*]Fixed bug where staff would wait literally forever to serve if there was food already on the serving station.
[*]Fixed a bug where the game would complain about there being no free chairs even though there were some.
[*]Fixed a bug where the customers would fail to use an object and then break when leaving.
[*]Fixed a bug where the hot take timer would stay on screen even though the hot take bonus was finished.
[*]Many other small fixes.
[/list]

In addition Hipster Café is 20% off for the Steam summer sale right now! 

Onto something more personal. When I decided to make Hipster Café, I had already been growing my hipster hair bun for quite a while. In fact the Scandi-hipster in the game may bear more than a passing resemblance to yours truly.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/8069dda11a599a43eff1ce4fce76ef8bf7caee40.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/5c2adc4205748df1861c46f465c80a1c42d2679f.jpg[/img]

I started telling people that I wouldn't cut my hair until I had released the new game. The only problem is, that was in [b]2018[/b], and the hipster bun kept growing. Games are a lot harder to make than you'd think!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/e0f94ac404d584ade92835bda2523bf3ddddb198.jpg[/img]

Now the game has been out in Early Access for a while, and it was time to make good on my threat to cut my hair. The last time it met the scissors was actually in 2012, just around a decade ago, and by this point had reached a whooping 83cm length!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/c6cfa5cee0ccabcc818dfcf4126d8dba93264429.jpg[/img]

So this week, it was finally time to go to the hair dresser and get it chopped off. The hair has been donated to The Little Princess Trust who make wigs for children with cancer. You can help support their work here: [url=https://www.littleprincesses.org.uk/]https://www.littleprincesses.org.uk/[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/69af8ce8e119c4d6b3fa6984637d0bb1ac23576e.jpg[/img]

'til next time fellow hipsters!

notes.content:

Hello! I've just set the latest Early Access build live.
This one includes a bunch of changes and fixes suggested by our players in the first week of early access.
[list]
[*] Employees now have a chance to level up their skills when they do a task. It still takes them a while to master the art of shooing though!
[*] Changing the staff task settings should now save and load properly with your save game,
[*] All the different audio settings you choose should now stick from one session to another, if you don't like the sounds of the ocean, then you'll only have to turn it off once. Good riddance.
[*] Changing the decoration colours should now save properly with your save game.
[*] The menu requests now draw behind the mouse over tooltip, fixing some problems where it wasn't possible to read the tooltip.
[*] The tooltips for menu requests in the coffee / food makers are now a bit more informative.
[*] There will be at least a few toots about the trending hashtag when a hot topic start trending on Tooter.
[*] The music shouldn't get stuck on the same song anymore. I mean it was my favourite and I was going to play it on repeat forever anyway, but I guess you might want to hear a different one eventually.
[*] Plus a bunch of other small fixes & tweaks.

notes.title: Early Access Released
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/bbf439d3fd30c070833de837b43275b5e96e3c9b.jpg[/img]
Since launching the free demo of Hipster Café in Steam Next Fest in February, we've had an incredible amount of invaluable player feedback. We want to keep working with our players to make sure the game is the best it can be, and we think the right next step for that is to enter early access. With that in mind I've just set the Early Access version live on the store.

A huge amount of content is already in the game, but naturally for early access some systems will still receive more balancing, tweaks and bug fixes based on player feedback. 

Here are some of the things you can already do in the early access version:

[list]
[*]Build furniture, decorations, equipment and entertainment items from a list of over 220 items in your Hipster Café. Hipsters just wanna have fun.
[*]Make stupid food by combining 80 weird ingredients, serve it up on one of eight different "plates". [*]Manage your menu to impress over 30 different types of hipsters.
[*]From filter coffee to cold brew, adjust the flavour of 10 types of coffee, and impress the hipsters by drawing what they ask for with the latte art in their coffee.
[*]Keep up to date on the latest trends on social media. Send out a Toot with the right hashtags before the Hot Take timer goes out to gain bonus followers for your café!
[*]Research to unlock the improved entertainment items, better café equipment and more ingredients.
[*]Choose the colours and floors of your café, and design it's unique logo.
[*]Hire and manage your very own staff from more than 30 hireable characters.
[*]Call your dad when you run out of money, or just to ask "What's up?",
[/list]
The demo version will remain free for those who prefer to wait for a final release.

We are looking forward to getting more feedback from you all. You can continue to use the in game feedback button, the steam discussion boards or just email us at steam@usefulslug.com with your comments. 

Thank you so much to all the players that have given us feedback so far! You're awesome!

notes.title: Better staff tasks, more bug fixes and early access on the way.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/ca47bc18d800877457b0a38e254545a3d510bc3d.jpg[/img]
Over the past few weeks we've had the free demo available and the player feedback from that has proven invaluable in improving the game. However it's also clear that the game is not yet fully balanced and polished. 

We want to continue to work with our players to make sure the game is the best it can be, and we think the right next step for that is to enter early access. I've recently submitted the latest full content version for review by Valve and hope that will be ready for you all to play very soon. I appreciate that some of you have been waiting patiently for a [i]final [/i]version, but I hope you can understand that we believe working with the player feedback a bit longer will get us all the [i]best [/i]version of Hipster Café. 
The Demo version will remain free if you prefer to wait.

I've just set the latest version of the Demo live. This one includes a big bunch of bug fixes and improvements from player feedback.
[list]
[*] Customers shouldn't pepper the social media with pictures of their food quite as often. I wish I had this setting for Instagram too.
[*] Staff should now be able to research on multiple research stations at once if the technology is advanced enough.
[*] Events that previously removed a member of staff if you failed the missions now instead reduce their skills.
[*] Saving and loading games should now be a lot more robust.
[*] Fixed a number of issues where Tooter would render the messages strangely. 
[*] Removed some questionable/offensive content from the string builders that generate the Tooter content.
[*] Fixed a lot of staff issues where their equipment was moved or sold.
[*] Fixed a number of bugs with the in game feedback form.
[*] Plus many other minor bug fixes.
[/list]

I also found the source of a bug which breaks the coffee maker on [i]some[/i] computers. If this happens on your computer, you need to make sure you have installed bot the X86 and the X64 version of the Visual C++ Redistributable from Microsoft. You can find these here: 
[url=https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170]https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170[/url]

Special thanks to everyone who have provided feedback and bug reports. You're awesome!

notes.title: Graphics presets, performance and bug fixes.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/18d73043fe5c4f55e3c2ad03f56ca4c52ee95bfd.jpg[/img]
I've just set live the latest build of the Demo.

This update focused on making sure it was more easily playable on a range of computers, as well as performance and bug fixes. The game uses a dynamic form of lighting that bounces the light around and traces reflections in real time. Even though the game style perhaps looks simple, these lighting calculations can be quite heavy for the computer and will definitely make it lag if you have a less powerful graphics card. With the new presets and auto-detection features, it should make it much more smoother across a whole range of computers, without the player needing to know the ins and outs of complex global illumination settings!

Here are the main highlights:
[list]
[*] The game should now autodetect if you drop below 25 frames per second average, and suggest automatically detecting graphics settings if you do.
[*] You can also run the autodetect graphics settings from within the Video settings.
[*] There are also now 5 presets you can manually choose from, that will toggle a number of the video settings to give you gradually higher framerate while trading off visual accuracy. 
[*] Fixed a number of bugs related to placement on counters, especially after loading a game.
[*] Fixed a number of smaller bugs.
[/list]

Thank you again to everyone who have sent feedback via the in game and end of play feedback forms! You're awesome and have given me so much helpful feedback! 
Also big thanks to everyone who's streaming and making video reviews of the game. These are always really heart warming to see.

notes.title: Multi actions, save games and control customization in the brand new patch.
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/ba9742475bb76c70241e34ea7642831f02a3325e.jpg[/img]
Hey all, I've just set the latest patch of the demo live. This one addresses some bugs and some user feedback from the past few weeks.

Latest changes:
[list]
[*] You can queue up research now by pressing Shift + the stuff you want to research.
[*] You can also add more of the same type of furniture, by holding shift when you click to place it.
[*] And, hold my beer, you can even keep adding more of the same type of food by holding shift when clicking to place it.
[*] Space bar now toggles between play and pause.
[*] You can now customize more of the controls. Don't like rotating with the right mouse button? That's fine, you can rotate with any other button! Just change it in the settings. Space bar to play / pause? Why not try F8?
[*] Saving games should now work a lot better. By that I mean, it should work now, it was definitely broken in a large number of ways before. Loading old save games will almost certainly be broken. There may be other exotic ways it is broken too, but at least those are a novel experience.
[*] Scrolling with a mouse wheel should work more correctly in more places.
[/list]

Plus a bunch of smaller bug fixes. 
Big thanks to everyone helping me find bugs and providing feedback, you're awesome!

notes.title: Steam Next Fest And What's Next Best
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/8582769394283d102621bf4b6b1ccff044516b00.jpg[/img]
Steam Next Fest is over, and we want to thank everyone who played our demo! We got a bunch of feedback and bug reports through the online feedback form as well as the in game feedback form. Thank you so much to everyone who contributed. Also huge thanks to everyone who streamed the game, made videos or wrote about it. It's so important for indie games to get any kind of exposure to have a chance at survival. Big heart energy.

I've decided to keep the free demo live while I work on more of the bugs and keep balancing and tweaking the gameplay according to your feedback, and will be making updates to the demo build while we move towards release. Think of it as a kind of free early access period.

I've just uploaded another build with more tweaks based on player feedback from last week. There's a lot more to come in the coming weeks, and I'll aim to put a new build up each week or two. Some will have gameplay tweaks, some will be bug fixes.

The latest patch includes:
[list]
[*] Significantly increased the amount of time between changing hipster types, let us know if it's still too fast. 
[*] Fixed bugs related to running tutorials more than once, so if you didn't quite catch something the first time, that's like A-OK with the game now. 
[*] Fixed a number of smaller bugs related to Tooter content generation. 
[/list]


This adds to the two patches from last week:
[list]
[*] Hipsters will now use the same entertainment item twice, if they have more than one of the same need. I don't remember why I thought this was a fun idea in the first place, but based on player feedback, you didn't. So it's changed now.
[*] You don't need to pay the staff as much. Don't worry, most of them have their own trust fund and are just doing this as a side-hustle until the band takes off.
[*] Tutorials should enable all the menus that it's trying to highlight, and keep the menu accessible.
[*] Dad should now provide you with money if you run out. All you've got to do is call him. Your mum asks if you've tried using "Social media" for your café.
[*] You can now move something on top of a counter, and then put it back in the same place. I'm not sure why you want to do that, but you couldn't before, and I got quite a lot of bug reports about it! (Actually thanks a lot for the bug reports, you're awesome!)
[*] Having more than 1 staff should be much more stable now. Terry still isn't stable though, he had a bit too much wine yesterday and keeps going on about his headache.
[*] Fixed a bunch of minor exceptions that could have caused other instabilities.
[/list]

notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/32576704/c0bba7df6e23674a0c9b62189d5dc75f523034da.jpg[/img]
Steam Next Fest is about to begin. If you have a friend who you think might enjoy Hipster Café, please send them a link. The more people that try it, and the more feedback I get on the game, the better it will be in the long run.

I've just uploaded a patch containing a few minor bugfixes. It should download automatically if you have the demo installed.
[list]
[*] Dad should now provide you with money if you run out. All you've got to do is call him. Your mum asks if you've tried using "Social media" for your café.
[*] You can now move something on top of a counter, and then put it back in the same place. I'm not sure why you want to do that, but you couldn't before, and I got quite a lot of bug reports about it! (Actually thanks a lot for the bug reports, you're awesome!)
[*] Having more than 1 staff should be much more stable now. Terry still isn't stable though, he had a bit too much wine yesterday and keeps going on about his headache.
[*] Fixed a bunch of minor exceptions that could have caused other instabilities.
[/list]

notes.title: Zune Update
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/ae6ac8818d34d61c78dae764c27c7b9c9a65fbe7.jpg[/img]
[h1]OHAI[/h1]

Unlike the Zune, we're not actually dead, and have been hard at work since showcasing our prototype at Rezzed last year. We're a bit behind schedule, but wanted to give you guys an update showing some of the things we've been adding to the game since we last showed it.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/b912ef9017e2ac8a4f6bd176edc94568dffbb6f3.jpg[/img]
[h1]Entertainment[/h1]
Are you not entertained?! Neither are the hipsters, but they want to be. They now have needs, such as music, artsy and physical entertainment, that should be satisfied before they go to get their grub.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/7aa095b40cff362005b305ec271fbfaecc8ebf21.png[/img]
[h1][url=https://www.reddit.com/r/WeWantPlates/]We want plates[/url][/h1]
Anyone can serve food on a plate. What will really set your hipster cafe apart? How about putting the chips in a mug? Is fast food even faster when it's on a skateboard?

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/d4aa489eb0459480e697986db794e8820bc5362c.jpg[/img]
[h1]Research tree[/h1]
Your staff need to discover what the latest food blog trend is by spending time on social media. At least we put to bed the question of what came first, chicken or the egg. It was the egg.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/5dad5ce92015ea4162fe7fa0c5de5748c8158504.jpg[/img]
[h1]Expansions[/h1]
If your cafe is going to be successful, you will need to expand. Pricing out the local community is a good way of doing that. No one is going to remember the orphanage or the animal rescue center that used to be there when they hear about your avochinos.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/32576704/c39bf3f4c20eeb6b9427014bbcf06c56939de5bc.jpg[/img]
[h1]Trend stock market[/h1]
Keeping track of the current trends is important, but once something goes mainstream, don't expect it to stay cool for long.

We've still got a lot of work to do on the game, and it can be tricky to say how long everything will take and we don't yet have a specific release date, but we'll try to update more often going forward.
